notesStmt.note: The date written at the bottom of this manuscript indicates that Whitman had begun drafting the poem at least by mid-summer, several months before he submitted it for publication. For further details about his attempts to sell this and other poems to magazines, see the editorial note for loc.00229.

"Sail Out for Good, Eidólon Yacht" was first published in the March 1891 issue of Lippincott's Magazine, in a group of poems collectively titled "Old-Age Echoes." It was later included in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891).

lg.l:
O little white-hulled sloop, now really speed
me on ‸really on deep waters,
(I will not call it our? my concluding voyage,

But ‸real outset and sure entrance to the truest,
best, maturest,)

Depart! depart from solid earth — no more re–
turningreturning
to these shores,
